claims.text: Niobium and tantalum are superconducting elements.
A refractory high-entropy alloy containing Nb and Ta can exhibit superconductivity.
The conventional superconductivity associated with Nb and Ta can be preserved in a disordered, high-mixing-entropy matrix.
The resulting superconducting phase may have robust flux-pinning characteristics.
A near-equiatomic Nb-Ta-based refractory HEA with additional refractory elements can form a single-phase solid solution at room temperature.
Cooling the alloy below its superconducting transition temperature will permit entry into a superconducting state.
High mixing entropy stabilizes a disordered solid-solution structure in the proposed alloy.
The disordered solid solution uniformly distributes Nb and Ta atoms among the other refractory elements.
Electron-phonon coupling involving Nb and Ta leads to Cooper-pair formation in the alloy.
Intrinsic lattice disorder may enhance flux pinning.
Intrinsic lattice disorder may modify the superconducting transition temperature.
Below a critical temperature, the alloy will exhibit zero electrical resistance.
Below a critical temperature, the alloy will expel magnetic fields through the Meissner effect.
The proposed HEA has a random solid-solution microstructure.
The proposed HEA exhibits normal resistive behavior at room temperature.
Significantly lowering the concentrations of Nb and Ta may suppress or eliminate the superconducting transition.
Adding elements that produce strong pair-breaking effects may suppress or eliminate the superconducting transition.

contradictions.description: The structure is described as a random solid solution with Nb and Ta uniformly distributed among other elements, while the mechanism invokes a distinct Nb/Ta sublattice; a chemically random solution does not necessarily contain an Nb/Ta-specific sublattice.
